title: Compatible trivializations of finite derived local systems
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $(B_n)_{n\geq1}$ an inverse sequence of finite commutative rings with surjective maps $q_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Let $K_n\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B_n)$ and $E_n\in D(B_n)$ be bounded complexes with finite locally constant cohomology and finite module cohomology respectively [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Supply normalization isomorphisms $\rho_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{B_{n+1}}B_n\simeq K_n$ and $\eta_n:E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{B_{n+1}}B_n\simeq E_n$, with their quotient cocycles [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Assume the sheaf of derived isomorphisms $\mathcal I_n=\operatorname{Isom}(\underline E_n,K_n)$, defined by sheafifying isomorphisms on etale localized sites, is finite locally constant and has nonempty stalks. Reduction defines $r_n:\mathcal I_{n+1}\to\mathcal I_n$ by $e\mapsto\rho_n\circ(e\otimes^L B_n)\circ\underline{\eta_n}^{-1}$. Then there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_j\to X\}_j$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and isomorphisms $e_{jn}:\underline E_n|_{U_j}\simeq\nu_X^*K_n|_{U_j}$ such that $r_n(e_{j,n+1})=e_{jn}$ for all $n$. Here the displayed constant complexes and reduction maps are pulled to the pro-etale site by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. No surjectivity of the original $r_n$ is required.

proof.text: Work over each affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$; these opens cover $X$. The hypotheses on $\mathcal I_n$ restrict to $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-sets-representability] choose finite etale $P_n\to V$ and isomorphisms $h_{P_n}\cong\mathcal I_n|_V$, where $h_{P_n}(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_V(W,P_n)$. Use [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ to turn $r_n$ into a $V$-map $p_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$: it is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{P_{n+1}}$ under the corresponding natural transformation. Naturality says that every value of this transformation is postcomposition with $p_n$, so all iterated reduction maps correspond to the composites of the $p_n$. No surjectivity of $p_n$ is asserted.

proof.text: Write $P_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ (finite morphisms are affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]). Form $C=\varinjlim_n A_n$ in commutative $A$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist], with transitions $p_n^\#$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] identifies $P=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $\varprojlim_n P_n$, with projections $\pi_n$ satisfying $p_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$. Every $A_n$ is etale over $A$, so $A\to C$ is ind-etale by its definition, and [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes $P\to V$ weakly etale. Open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; their local ring maps and their diagonals are isomorphisms, hence flat, so they are weakly etale by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. The stability node therefore makes $P\to X$ weakly etale by composition. The countable diagram and its colimit are small in the fixed universe: the colimit is a quotient of a set of finite words in the disjoint union of the $A_n$. Thus $P$ is a legitimate affine pro-etale site object.

Fix $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$. Put $S_n=(\mathcal I_n)_{\bar v}$, finite and nonempty by hypothesis. For $m\geq n$ let $r_{m,n}$ be the composite stalk transition and put $T_n=\bigcap_{m\geq n}\operatorname{im}(r_{m,n})$. These are nonempty: the images are nested nonempty subsets of the finite $S_n$, hence eventually constant. The restricted map $T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is surjective: given $t\in T_n$, choose $m\geq n+1$ beyond stabilization for both levels, lift $t$ to $s\in S_m$, and take $r_{m,n+1}(s)\in T_{n+1}$. Apply [lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective] to the $T_n$ to choose a compatible tuple $(t_n)$. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], each $t_n$ is a germ represented by a section on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$. Under $\mathcal I_n|_V\cong h_{P_n}$ this section is a map $W\to P_n$; composing with $\bar w$ gives an $\Omega$-point of $P_n$. This depends only on the germ, since two representatives of the same germ agree on a common pointed refinement. It commutes with $r_n$ and $p_n$ by the postcomposition description in step 1. The resulting compatible $\Omega$-points give $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ by the limit property in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit]. Every point of $V$ admits a geometric point, so $P\to V$ is surjective. Being affine and weakly etale, it is a singleton pro-etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; on any affine open $V'\subset V$, its inverse image is affine and surjects onto $V'$, giving the required finite covering witness.

proof.text: Let $a_n\in\mathcal I_n(P_n)$ be the universal section corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{P_n}$. The explicit presheaf-colimit formula of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], at the pair $(P_n,\pi_n:P\to P_n)$, gives a section $s_n\in(\nu_X^*\mathcal I_n)(P)$ after sheafification. Its reduction is represented by $r_n(a_{n+1})$, which corresponds to $p_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$. In that colimit it equals the image of $a_n$ along this arrow; since $p_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$, it is exactly $s_n$. Consequently $(\nu_X^*r_n)(s_{n+1})=s_n$ for every $n$. This construction uses the actual universal projections and gives one simultaneous compatible tuple, without taking a limit through the inverse-image functor.

source.place: Tag 09BV, lemma-weird, compatible sections; explicit inverse-image colimit and universal projections

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family] in the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $P$. It gives a covering $\{U_j\to P\}$ with affine $U_j$ weakly contractible for this full site. Compose with the singleton cover $P\to V$, and then with the affine open covering of $X$. This gives the required covering of $X$. Pull back the sections $s_n$ to each $U_j$; the same compatibility equations still hold, since restrictions commute with sheaf morphisms.

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-isomorphism-sheaf-wcontractible-evaluation] with $B=B_n,E=E_n,K=K_n$ on each $U_j$. Its isomorphism bijection turns $s_n|_{U_j}$ into an actual derived isomorphism $e_{jn}:\underline E_n|_{U_j}\simeq(\nu_X^*K_n)|_{U_j}$. All boundedness and finiteness assumptions are the supplied levelwise assumptions. For scalar extension $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, the resulting objects are bounded because they identify with $E_n,K_n$ through $\eta_n,\rho_n$. The natural tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies the pulled-back etale reduction with the pro-etale derived reduction. By the bridge's scalar-extension and composition clauses, the section $(\nu_X^*r_n)(s_{n+1}|_{U_j})$ corresponds precisely to
$\rho_n|_{U_j}\circ(e_{j,n+1}\otimes^L_{B_{n+1}}B_n)\circ(\underline{\eta_n}|_{U_j})^{-1}$.
Since it equals $s_n|_{U_j}$, injectivity of the bridge's bijection gives that displayed composite equal to $e_{jn}$, which is the asserted compatibility. The empty $X$ is handled by the empty covering. Bounds need not be uniform in $n$, and neither the original reductions nor the scheme projections need be surjective.

split_report.summary: Represented the finite isomorphism sheaves, constructed an affine ind-etale inverse limit, proved its surjectivity from stable finite stalk images, and refined it by weakly contractible affines.
